successors.name: Neo-Hittite states
successors.text: the Syro-Hittite states of south-east Anatolia and north-west Syria, led by 'Karkemiš under Kuzi-Teššub'

ledger.x: c. 1650 BC: Labarna I, who renamed himself Hattusili I, makes Hattusa his capital. The infobox gives the establishment as c. 1650 BC and the text has him 'sometime around 1650 BC and established his capital city at Hattusa'. The page gives the city, not a boundary; the kingdom grew out of Kussara and Kanesh (Neša), a…

c. 1400 BC: the court withdraws to Šamuḫa. The infobox lists it as capital-in-exile '(1400–1350 BC)', 'In exile under Tudḫaliya III'; the Middle Kingdom court had already moved to Sapinuwa (no years).

c. 1400 BC: Tudhaliya I builds the first empire. 'Tudhaliya I (c. 1400 BC) vanquished the Hurrian states of Aleppo and Mitanni' and 'expanded to the west at the expense of Arzawa'; Kizzuwatna was allied with the Hittites under Telipinu and Tudhaliya I (the page's words, unquoted). Cliopatria's step adds 109,000 km2…
c. 1350 BC: the court returns to Hattusa. The page ends the exile at 1350 ('(1400–1350 BC)') and does not describe the return.
1345 BC: Suppiluliuma I's Syrian war takes Mitanni's western lands.

c. 1345 BC (bridged): the rest of Syria falls to Suppiluliuma I. The page says Kadesh's king Šutatarra was defeated, Nuḫašši's king driven out, Qatna among 'the Syrian kingdoms he conquered after crossing the Euphrates', but gives no year; 1345 is the Mitanni page's date of the war, and his reign is 'c. 1350–1322 BC'.
c. 1345 BC (bridged): Ugarit recognises Hittite suzerainty. King Niqmaddu II recognised Suppiluliuma's suzerainty (the page's statement, no year; reign 'c. 1350–1322 BC').

c. 1345 BC (bridged): Amurru passes from Egypt to the Hittites. The Suppiluliuma page says Amurru's king Aziru defied Egypt and became a Hittite vassal (no year). Ramesses II recovered it in the 1270s (see the contest below).

c. 1330 BC: Shattiwaza is installed as king of what was left of Mitanni. Shattiwaza was installed by a Hittite army 'in the late 14th century BC' and 'reigned c. 1330–1305 BC' (Mitanni page); the country became 'alternately the dependency of the Hittites and the Assyrians' (Suppiluliuma page).
1327 BC: Carchemish falls.

c. 1305 BC (bridged): Mitanni passes to Assyrian suzerainty. Shattiwaza's reign ends c. 1305 and 'Adad-nirari claims to have captured King Shattuara and brought him to Ashur, where he took an oath as a vassal' (Mitanni page, no year).

c. 1300 BC (bridged): Mursili II settles the west. He turned west to resist Uhhaziti, king of Arzawa (page's words, unquoted), and the page lists treaties with Mira-Kuwaliya, Hapalla and the Seha River Land; the page gives no year (reign 1321-1295 on the page's short chronology). 1300 is Cliopatria's step. The 440…

c. 1300 BC (bridged): the Arzawa lands are Hittite vassals. The Mursili II page lists treaties with Kupanta-Kurunta (Mira-Kuwaliya), Targašnalli (Hapalla) and Manapa-Tarhunta (Seha River Land); undated.
ledger.cp: Mira-Kuwaliya, Hapalla and the Seha River Land

ledger.x: c. 1275 BC (mirrored): Ramesses II retakes Amurru. The treaty page says only that the Hittites took Amurru during their Syrian campaigns (no year); the date and the loss are the Egyptian dossier's (Ramesses II in his fourth year). Page silent.
c. 1275 BC (mirrored): Amurru passes back to Egypt for a year (Egyptian dossier); page silent.

c. 1274 BC: Hittites and Egyptians meet at Kadesh. The treaty page puts the Battle of Kadesh around 1274 BC with neither side prevailing decisively, and says the Hittites took Amurru during their Syrian campaigns (no year); the Egyptian dossier has Ramesses II retaking Amurru c. 1275.
May 1274 BC (mirrored): after Kadesh the Hittites hold the Orontes valley.
1274 BC (mirrored): Amurru is again a Hittite vassal (the treaty page says the Hittites took Amurru during their campaigns, no year).
1258 BC: Hattusili III and Ramesses II make peace.

c. 1220 BC (bridged): Assyria takes ground from Tudhaliya IV. He 'was heavily defeated by Tukulti-Ninurta I of Assyria in the Battle of Nihriya' (reign c. 1245-1215, no year); the page names no land. The Assyrian dossier should carry the matching gain.
c. 1185 BC: Ugarit is destroyed in the collapse. The page calls it a 'small seagoing vassal state (destroyed c. 1185 BC)'.
c. 1180 BC: the vassalage ends with the empire.
c. 1180 BC: the western vassalage ends with the empire.
ledger.cp: Mira-Kuwaliya, Hapalla and the Seha River Land

ledger.x: c. 1180 BC: the south-east survives as the Neo-Hittite states. After Hattusa fell, 'Karkemiš under Kuzi-Teššub' expanded into a regional power; 'These Syro-Hittite states gradually fell under the control of the Neo-Assyrian Empire (911–608 BC)'.

c. 1180 BC: the plateau is stateless. The Sea Peoples began their 'push down the Mediterranean coastline' (Cilicia and Cyprus), with Kaskian, Phrygian and Bryges invasions and 'drought for three consecutive years in 1198, 1197 and 1196 BC'; Hattusa 'burnt to the ground sometime around 1180 BC'; by 1160 'much of the…

c. 1180 BC: the Hittite Empire ends. Suppiluliuma II's reign 'began in c. 1207 BC and ended coinciding with the collapse of the Hittite Empire'; the infobox says disestablished c. 1200 BC, the text has Hattusa abandoned c. 1190 and burnt c. 1180. wars.name: Hittite raid on Aleppo and Babylon
wars.outcome: Mursili I 'conducted a great raid down the Euphrates River, bypassing Assyria and sacking Aleppo and Babylon'; no land was held and he was murdered on his return.

wars.name: Great Syrian War (Suppiluliuma I against Mitanni)
wars.outcome: Hittite victory: Washukanni sacked in 1345, Carchemish taken 1327, Mitanni reduced to a Hittite dependency under Shattiwaza.

wars.name: Mursili II's Arzawa campaign
wars.outcome: Arzawa defeated and its lands bound to the Hittites by treaties with Mira-Kuwaliya, Hapalla and the Seha River Land.

wars.name: Hittite-Egyptian war over Kadesh and Amurru
Hittite-Assyrian war under Tudhaliya IV (Battle of Nihriya)
wars.outcome: Tudhaliya IV 'heavily defeated by Tukulti-Ninurta I of Assyria'; the shape loses 20,000 km2 between 1240 and 1220 (attribution bridged).

wars.name: Collapse of the Hittite Empire
wars.outcome: The empire ends: Hattusa abandoned c.
